verdict.rationale: Sumsub's own Summy AI Level Builder lets users create and configure verification levels by describing requirements in plain language, so the product natively takes natural-language commands. That is limited to one workflow. The official MCP server also lets external AI agents perform Sumsub operations, but that depends on a third-party agent rather than a built-in natural-language interface. Missing for 10: natural-language control beyond level building (e.g. applicant review actions, AML settings, webhooks) inside the product itself, documentation of the scope of actions available by command, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: It helps you create and configure verification levels quickly and effortlessly by just describing your requirements in plain language.
Use the MCP server to let AI agents perform Sumsub operations on your behalf, while keeping access controlled by your existing Sumsub role permissions.
